title: Separate messaging semantics from transport
purpose: A messaging replacement changes more than a connection string. For developers who understand the booking flow, this chapter follows that flow through NATS and asks what publishing, reconnecting and recording a business result each establish.
entryAssumptions: The PostgreSQL state still uses the earlier messaging transport.
concepts: A subject names an event channel. Publishing, receiving and committing a business change are separate events; transport availability alone does not guarantee replay or exactly-once processing.
runtimePrerequisites: Use the state quickstart for tool versions, generation, start and stop commands. Run one local state at a time because ports and generated output directories are shared.

transitions.carriesForward: Move persistence to PostgreSQL while retaining account, trade and position behavior.
transitions.motivation: The PostgreSQL state still uses the earlier messaging transport.
transitions.increment: Replace internal messaging with NATS while preserving the trade-to-position workflow.
transitions.evidence: NATS carries the internal event while the business result remains recognizable. Subject names and payload fields determine interoperability. Reconnection establishes a new connection, not proof of recovery of every missed event. Check the configured messaging mode before making delivery claims.

walkthrough.action: Start this state, run the quickstart smoke checks, and trace one small trade through the messaging subject map and publisher/subscriber code. Record the trade identifier in the resulting trade and position views.

walkthrough.action: In a disposable demo, restart the NATS service identified in Compose and observe subscriber reconnection. Compare a trade submitted after recovery with prior records; do not assume events sent during an outage are replayed.
walkthrough.expected: Reconnection establishes a new connection, not proof of recovery of every missed event. Check the configured messaging mode before making delivery claims.

assessments.question: What evidence distinguishes broker recovery from business recovery?
assessments.guidance: Show the connection returning and separately reconcile the relevant trade identifiers and positions. State the configured delivery limitations.

limitations: Reconnection establishes a new connection, not proof of recovery of every missed event. Check the configured messaging mode before making delivery claims.
This is an educational local demonstration. Passing its checks does not establish production readiness, financial settlement, or correctness under every failure mode.

coaching.diagnosticQuestion: How does an event connect trade submission to the processor in the previous state?
coaching.predictionPrompt: Predict whether reconnecting a subscriber proves that every event from an outage was recovered.
hints: Trace the event subject and payload rather than stopping at the broker connection.
Check the configured delivery mode and reconcile the business records for the relevant identifiers.
coaching.misconception: Broker connectivity proves replay, exactly-once processing or a completed business result.
coaching.evidenceToRequest: Ask for the subject/payload route, reconnection evidence and matching persisted trade/position; keep any unobserved outage result unknown.
